headline: India's retail securitisation market grew 42% to Rs 1.46 lakh crore in H1 FY27
hook: Gold and vehicle loans drive securitisation growth
summary: India's retail securitisation market expanded by 42 percent to reach Rs 1.46 lakh crore in the first half of fiscal year 2027, according to a report by Crisil Ratings. This growth was primarily fueled by an increasing share of gold loans and vehicle loans within the sector. Securitisation allows lenders to pool and sell retail loans, freeing up capital to issue new credit. For Indian retail investors, this trend highlights robust credit demand and shifting asset quality in non-banking financial companies.
whats_next: Full-year credit growth and asset quality reports
why_it_matters: Higher loan pooling boosts liquidity for lenders and credit growth.
winners_losers: Gold loan NBFCs gain / traditional lenders face competition

headline: CRISIL credit ratio improves to 2.18x with bank growth seen at 14.5-15.5%
hook: Strong credit ratio and steady banking growth projected
summary: CRISIL's credit ratio has improved to 2.18x, reflecting better borrower health across rated entities. This trend indicates sustained lending demand and stable asset quality in the financial sector. Indian retail investors should monitor banking stocks as credit expansion drives sector earnings.
